## King Maker Authority-Site ROI Model — NC Roofing Contractor
**Every number below is MODELED.** Tickets and close-rate bands are sourced from the digest; lead volumes are a marked assumption (no absolute baseline exists in the sources); all revenue and delta figures are model outputs.

| Input | Conservative | Realistic | Optimistic | Source / Type |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Monthly qualified leads | 3 | 6 | 12 | **MODELED ASSUMPTION** — no absolute baseline in digest; scaled on sourced ~1.5x-3x lead multiple & >2x-at-300-pages [P1][P5][P2] |
| Close rate (lead→job) | 15% | 20% | 25% | Sourced band 18-24% [P10]; low pushed below floor, high rounded up — MODELED on sourced band |
| Jobs / month | ~0.45 | ~1.2 | ~3.0 | MODELED (leads × close) |
| Jobs / year | ~5.4 | ~14.4 | ~36 | MODELED |
| Avg ticket (revenue) | $9,500 | $12,000 | $18,000 | $9.5k measured (NerdWallet) [P3]; $12k/$18k modeled tiers [P10] |
| Value per lead (rev) | ~$1,425 | ~$2,400 | ~$4,500 | MODELED (ticket × close) [P10] |
| **Annual revenue (matured)** | **$51,300** | **$172,800** | **$648,000** | **MODELED** |
| − One-time build | −$5,000 | −$5,000 | −$5,000 | Task spec |
| − Annual ops ($500/mo) | −$6,000 | −$6,000 | −$6,000 | Task spec; low end of pro market (avg ~$1,557/mo) [P4] |
| **Δ vs GHL $297/mo template (Yr-1, ramp-adj)** | **≈ +$34,300** | **≈ +$95k–$110k** | **≈ +$300k+** | **MODELED Year-1, ~30-40% cold-start haircut [P10]** |
| **Δ vs GHL template (matured run-rate)** | **+$40,300** | **+$161,800** | **+$637,000** | **MODELED steady-state (12-24+ mo)** |

**How to read this:** The conservative row is engineered to be pessimistic — sub-band close rate (15% vs sourced 18-24% floor), the lowest sourced ticket ($9,500), only 3 leads/mo, and a ~30% Year-1 ramp haircut — and it *still* clears the $5k + $6k/yr cost in Year 1. The realistic row uses the digest's own value-per-lead figure ($2,400 = $12k × 20%) verbatim [P10]. The optimistic row stacks every input at its sourced ceiling (storm-active year, matured rankings, insurance-tier tickets) and is a low-probability upper bound, not a forecast.

**Why the delta exists at all (the mechanism, not the magnitude):** a $297/mo CSR template is structurally SEO-capped — 0 SSR/prerender [P5], AI-uncitable (crawlers read raw HTML only) [P5], no programmatic city pages [P5], and exposed to Google's site-wide thin-content drag if it clones geo-pages [P1][P9]. The authority site out-earns it by harvesting long-tail (one deep page ranks top-10 for ~1,000 keywords [P1]) and unlocking organic blue-link in cities with no office [P2]. Mechanism = well-sourced; per-client magnitude = modeled.

**Hard guardrails:** close rate is on the *client's* sales process, not the site (≈45% of home-services calls go unanswered [P7]); rankings are never guaranteed (Google now refers deceived businesses to the FTC [P11], and NC UDTPA carries treble damages [P11]); these are MODELED ranges, not promises.

hooks.hook: One real page out-ranks a hundred fake ones.
hooks.backingClaim: The average top-ranking page also ranks in the top 10 for ~1,000 other relevant keywords — one substantive page harvests hundreds of long-tail variations a boilerplate page cannot.
hooks.honestFraming: Organic long-tail reach, not a map-pack play. The ~1,000-keyword figure is the measured average for top-ranking pages, not a promise for any single page.

hooks.hook: Swap the city name. If the page still reads fine, Google already knows it's fake.
hooks.backingClaim: The 'delete the city name' test: if swapping the location leaves the rest of the copy valid, the page is boilerplate and fails Google's doorway/scaled-content policy. Genuine location pages need local proof and main-nav links.
hooks.honestFraming: Qualitative anti-doorway gate paired with Google's stated doorway/scaled-content spam policy, not a measured ranking score.

hooks.hook: Thin pages don't just fail. They drag down the good pages too.
hooks.backingClaim: Google's own guidance: unhelpful/templated content triggers a site-wide classifier that makes a site's OTHER good pages less likely to rank — weighted, so more unhelpful means a bigger hit.
hooks.honestFraming: Google's documented helpful-content mechanism, not a measured penalty figure. This is the ceiling on a boilerplate city-page matrix.

hooks.hook: Most contractors don't rank because most contractors ship template pages.
hooks.backingClaim: Across 1,400+ firms, companies crossing ~300+ indexed pages had median leads more than 2x the prior band, and +50-100 indexed pages drove double-digit lead growth.
hooks.honestFraming: Independent-ish leads dataset, but correlation not causation and vendor-sourced. Holds only when pages are unique/helpful — a 300-page doorway clone fails the helpful-content classifier instead.

hooks.hook: A page can rank you in a city you'll never set foot in.
hooks.backingClaim: Dedicated service-area pages let a contractor rank organically (blue-link) in cities where it has no office.
hooks.honestFraming: Organic blue-link only — NOT the map pack. Google's local algorithm only ranks businesses close to the searcher, so pages cannot win the pack in a city with no address.

hooks.hook: Proximity is most of the map pack. It's geometry you can't write your way out of.
hooks.backingClaim: Proximity to the searcher is the single dominant map-pack factor, weighted at roughly 55% in Whitespark's 2026 survey — more than all other factors combined.
hooks.honestFraming: Expert-survey weighting, directional not a controlled experiment. This is exactly why pages are an organic play and the pack is earned through GBP, proximity, and prominence.

hooks.hook: Hide your address and the map pack disappears. They tested it both ways.
hooks.backingClaim: Sterling Sky measured address-gating across 8,186 businesses in 200 cities: hiding the address tanked rankings, restoring it recovered them — replicated across locations.
hooks.honestFraming: A real lever the client cannot fake — a physical address. Confirms proximity is structural, not something a website wins.

hooks.hook: A storm roof is a five-figure job. Three independent sources, not a marketing number.
hooks.backingClaim: A storm/insurance roof replacement is a five-figure job: ~$17,631 avg replacement 2025 (Verisk), $14,747 avg NC wind/hail claim (III), ~$9,500 avg / up to $46,000 (NerdWallet).
hooks.honestFraming: Confirmed by consumer cost data, carrier analytics, and insurance-institute claim averages — measured, not a vendor estimate.

hooks.hook: US roof claims crossed thirty billion in a year. The vertical isn't a trend.
hooks.backingClaim: Carrier-side Verisk data: $30B+ US roof claims in 2024, up ~30% since 2022, with roofing more than 25% of residential claim value.
hooks.honestFraming: Carrier data independent of any marketing vendor — confirms market size and structural growth, not a per-client lead promise.

hooks.hook: Build the service-area pages and you rank where you don't live. One roofer saw leads climb 340%.
hooks.backingClaim: A verified roofing case: service-area pages ranked the company in cities outside its locality and drove +340% leads, +109% traffic, +111% conversion over two years.
hooks.honestFraming: Single measured case study over two years — organic service-area pages, not the map pack. Directional for any one client, not a typical result.

hooks.hook: Deep pages beat thin pages by 2 to 4x on traffic. That's the honest range.
hooks.backingClaim: Contractor case studies cluster at ~2x-4x traffic and ~1.5x-3x leads for deep vs thin pages (Sapphire +220%/+160%, Kodescape +188%/+145%), with >2x median leads at 300+ pages independently across 1,400 firms.
hooks.honestFraming: Stated as a range, mostly single-vendor self-reported and conditional on unique helpful pages — directional, not a guaranteed multiple.

hooks.hook: GoHighLevel sites ship an empty shell to the crawlers that matter.
hooks.backingClaim: Major AI search crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, OAI-SearchBot) don't execute JavaScript — they read raw HTML only — so a fully client-side-rendered GHL site returns an empty shell, confirmed across 500M+ crawler fetches.
hooks.honestFraming: Measured across 500M+ AI-crawler fetches. AI citability is future-proofing, not today's volume — AI referral traffic is still ~1% of visits.

hooks.hook: GoHighLevel has no export. You don't own the site you paid for.
hooks.backingClaim: GoHighLevel has no supported website export — sites cannot be cleanly migrated to a real CMS, per GHL's own support portal.
hooks.honestFraming: A concrete ownership/switching-cost ceiling confirmed by GHL's own support docs, not a performance claim.

hooks.hook: Anyone who guarantees a #1 ranking is reciting the warning sign. Google wrote it.
hooks.backingClaim: Google's own SEO guidance states no one can guarantee a #1 ranking and warns to beware SEOs that guarantee rankings or claim a 'special relationship' with Google.
hooks.honestFraming: Verbatim primary Google guidance. Frames why King Maker never promises guaranteed rankings or top-3-in-90-days — the promise contradicts Google's own word.

hooks.hook: Half the calls to home-service businesses never reach a person.
hooks.backingClaim: Only ~55% of calls to home-services businesses are answered by a person; in Construction, the closest roofing proxy, 61% are answered — across 60M+ analyzed calls.
hooks.honestFraming: Measured across 60M+ AI-analyzed calls. Stated as the answered-rate, not the inflated '74% unanswered' headline, which is the high end of a wide vendor range.

hooks.hook: The map pack takes half the clicks. The site fights for what's left.
hooks.backingClaim: The map pack captures roughly 44-50% of clicks on local result pages — the single largest block, ahead of organic (~40%) and ads (~10%).
hooks.honestFraming: Defensible click-distribution data. The often-quoted '60-90% of roofing leads' is an unverified vendor estimate and is not stated as fact.

hooks.hook: Adding internal links lifted organic traffic 25%. They split-tested it.
hooks.backingClaim: A controlled split-test added internal links and saw a 25% organic-traffic uplift on category pages, with the linking pages also gaining 20%+.
hooks.honestFraming: Controlled A/B test — causal, not correlational. Range across tests runs +5% to +25%; the 25% is the top of that band.

hooks.hook: New pages don't rank fast. Under 2% reach the top 10 in a year.
hooks.backingClaim: Only 1.74% of newly published pages reach Google's top 10 within a year, 72.9% of top-10 pages are 3+ years old, and the average #1 page is 5 years old.
hooks.honestFraming: Measured. The honest reason SEO must be modeled cold-start to maturity, not flat from month one — sets realistic timelines instead of overpromising.

hooks.hook: AI recommends almost no one. Getting picked is 3 to 30x harder than ranking.
hooks.backingClaim: Being recommended by AI is 3-30x harder than ranking in traditional local search — ChatGPT recommended 1.2% of locations, Gemini 11%, Perplexity 7.4%, vs 35.9% appearing in Google's local 3-pack.
hooks.honestFraming: Measured. AI recommendation is a scarce, defensible position to build toward — future-proofing, not a current traffic channel (AI is still ~1% of visits).

hooks.hook: One closed roof pays the software three times over.
hooks.backingClaim: GoHighLevel runs $97/$297/$497 per month, and a single closed ~$10k roof clears the most-popular $297/mo tier (~$3,564/yr) roughly 3x over.
hooks.honestFraming: Modeled comparison — GHL price is primary, the ~$10k ticket is measured. Frames software cost as a rounding error against one job, not a profit claim.

hooks.hook: A false 'bank-level security' claim is illegal the moment you publish it. No breach required.
hooks.backingClaim: FTC liability for false security claims doesn't require a breach — the 'likely to cause' unfairness standard and the deception prong reach broken security promises on unmitigated vulnerabilities alone; NC's UDTPA adds mandatory treble damages plus fees.
hooks.honestFraming: Independent legal analysis of FTC enforcement posture plus NC statutory text. The reason King Maker positions on actions (OWASP-hardened) and never claims SOC 2 or bank-level.

hooks.hook: The default CMS passes Google's speed test 40% of the time. Built sites don't gamble.
hooks.backingClaim: Field data: WordPress passes Core Web Vitals on only ~40% of origins, below the 51% global average, while purpose-built platforms outperform it (Duda 73%, TYPO3 71%, Squarespace 60%).
hooks.honestFraming: CrUX field data across all origins per CMS — measured. A platform-tier comparison, not a guarantee any one site passes.

guardrails.ftcPosture: Position King Maker's value-prop copy on ACTIONS we actually take, never on attestations or outcomes we cannot control. The FTC's own substantiation doctrine requires a "reasonable basis" of objective evidence to exist BEFORE any objective claim is published — failure to possess it "constitutes an unfair and deceptive act or practice in violation of Section 5" at the moment of dissemination, independent of outcome. That means a "we'll rank you" or "bank-level / SOC 2" claim is a violation the instant it goes live, with no breach and no failed ranking required: the FTC's deception prong reaches broken security promises on unmitigated vulnerabilities alone, and its unfairness "likely to cause" standard reaches risk rather than realized injury (Alston / Wyndham line). Google itself now hardens both flanks — its first-party SEO guidance states no one can guarantee a #1 ranking and warns to beware SEOs that guarantee rankings or claim a special relationship with Google, and it explicitly directs deceived businesses to file an FTC complaint (ftc.gov / 1-877-FTC-HELP). On top of federal exposure, NC's UDTPA (§ 75-1.1) makes deceptive commercial acts unlawful and § 75-16 mandates treble (3x) damages plus attorneys' fees on a proven violation — tripling a Charlotte/Raleigh roofing client's liability for any false claim we put in their mouth. The operative posture: every magnitude is a sourced, screenshot-provable, attributed range (vendor figures labeled vendor-reported and directional, independent figures labeled correlational), every security statement describes a concrete practice we performed (OWASP-hardened, zero stored data, prerendered HTML), and every ranking statement describes mechanism and earned probability over time — never a promised position, date, or guarantee.
neverClaim: "We win you the map pack" / "our website wins you the pack" — the pack is earned via GBP (~32%), reviews (~20%), proximity (~55% weight) and prominence; on-page site signals are only ~15% and falling. The site SUPPORTS the pack indirectly via links/prominence; it does not WIN it.

"Win the pack with pages" / city-page matrix wins the 3-pack — service-area pages can rank organically (blue-link) in no-office cities but cannot enter the map pack there, because proximity to the searcher dominates local ranking. This is an ORGANIC play, not a map-pack play.

"Our AI floods you with leads" / AI-lead-flood — AI referral traffic is ~1% of all website visits today and being AI-recommended is 3-30x HARDER than ranking in traditional local search. AI is a defensible scarce position to earn, not a lead firehose.

"Guaranteed rankings" / "guaranteed #1" / "guaranteed top-3 in 90 days" — Google's own guidance states no one can guarantee a #1 ranking and to beware SEOs that do; only 1.74% of new pages reach top-10 within a year and the average #1 page is ~5 years old. A dated ranking guarantee contradicts Google's first-party word and is an FTC/UDTPA violation at publication.

"SOC 2" / "bank-level security" / "compliant" / "certified" / "HIPAA" — never claim an attestation we don't literally hold; the FTC actions false security claims independent of any breach (Wyndham line), and the claim is actionable the moment it's published.

Any unsourced magnitude stated as fact — e.g. "60-90% of roofing leads come from the map pack" (vendor, unverified, inconsistent with the ~44-50%-of-clicks data), "$3-5k per lead" as typical (holds only at the storm/premium ceiling; realistic VPL ~$2,400 revenue), "74.1% of calls go unanswered" as consensus (it's the high end of a 27%-74% range), or any ROI multiple quoted as a promise. State every magnitude as a sourced, attributed range with the source class labeled.

"We guarantee leads / revenue / ROI" / promised return multiples — the ~681% / 5-month-breakeven figures are a single vendor's own un-third-party-verified client data with an assumed agency cost baked in; present directionally, never as a promised return.

sayInstead.ofClaiming: "Our website wins you the map pack."
sayInstead.instead: "The pack is earned through your Google Business Profile, reviews, and proximity — roughly 52% of the weight. Our site supports it indirectly through links and prominence; we build the GBP-linked landing and the ops layer that feed it."

sayInstead.ofClaiming: "City pages put you in the map pack across every town."

"AI referral traffic is about 1% of web visits today and being AI-recommended is 3-30x harder than ranking in normal local search — so we build clean, prerendered, semantic HTML now to earn that scarce, defensible position before it matters."

"No one can guarantee a ranking — Google says so directly and warns about anyone who claims otherwise. What we guarantee is the build: deep, helpful, schema-complete pages that compound, on a fast architecture that AI crawlers and Google can actually read. New pages typically take months, not days, to mature."
